extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians and policy-makers interested in positive psychology interventions and mental health promotion
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating randomized controlled trials of positive psychology interventions (PPIs) on subjective well-being, psychological well-being and depressive symptoms, with subgroup/moderator analyses and recommendations for practice and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: Subjective well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjective well-being was one of three primary outcomes studied (measured with instruments such as SWLS, PA, SHS, AF-1, GA, WB6, SHI, LSI-A etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report standardized effect sizes (Cohen's d) with 95% CI for subjective well-being; assess heterogeneity (I2, Q, T2) and check for publication bias. The meta-analysis reports a pooled post-test effect d = 0.34 (95% CI [0.22, 0.45]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: Psychological well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: Psychological well-being (e.g., Ryff’s Scales of Psychological Well-being, RPWB) was a primary outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Cohen's d with 95% CI and heterogeneity statistics; the pooled post-test effect reported was d = 0.20 (95% CI [0.09, 0.30]). Consider recalculation after addressing publication bias (Trim and Fill).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome: Depressive symptoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Depression symptom levels (measured with BDI, CES-D, HRSD, ZSRS, GDS, etc.) were a primary outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effect sizes and heterogeneity; pooled post-test effect reported d = 0.23 (95% CI [0.09, 0.38]). Follow-up effects may be non-significant; examine heterogeneity (I2 reported 47.0% for depression).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) only
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion was limited to randomized controlled trials; effectiveness estimates were derived from RCTs only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RCT designs where possible to reduce bias; adherence to CONSORT reporting is recommended. Note that RCT-only inclusion can produce smaller pooled effect sizes compared with mixes of study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of randomization procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomization procedure must be clearly reported; many included studies had unclear randomization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score quality negatively when randomization is not reported. Clear randomization reporting improves quality rating and confidence in effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis approach: intention-to-treat vs completers-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Many studies conducted completers-only analyses rather than intention-to-treat, which can seriously bias results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer and report intention-to-treat analyses; penalize studies that only report completers-only analyses when assessing quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rating (study quality scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies were rated on a quality scale with categories None, Low (1–2), Medium (3–4), High (5–6); no study met all quality criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an explicit multi-item quality scoring system; note that higher quality studies tended to show smaller effect sizes (quality rating moderated depression outcomes). Be conservative (give negative scores when criteria not reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration was categorized (<=4 weeks, <=8 weeks, >8 weeks); duration moderated effects (longer duration associated with larger effects on depression in meta-regression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing PPIs, prefer interventions at least four weeks and preferably eight weeks or longer to increase effectiveness. Report duration clearly in study methods and subgroup analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type/format of intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention format categories included self-help, group, and individual; format moderated effects (individual interventions showed larger effects, particularly for depression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report delivery format. For greater effectiveness, consider individual face-to-face delivery rather than unguided self-help, especially for clinical or psychosocially impacted populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment method
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruitment sources were coded (community, internet, referral/hospital, university, organization); recruitment method moderated outcomes (referral/hospital recruitment linked to larger effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recruitment pathways; consider recruiting via health care referrals when aiming for larger clinical effects. Internet/university recruitment may yield different effect sizes and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-selection vs not self-selected samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies were classified by whether participants were self-selected or not; self-selection was examined as a moderator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how participants were enrolled (self-selected vs referred/assigned). Self-selection can bias effect estimates and should be analyzed as a moderator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population characteristics and target group
rubrics_metrics.description: Population descriptors included adult, college students, older adults, clinical vs non-clinical; targeting people with psychosocial problems increased effect sizes for depression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify sample characteristics and inclusion criteria. Consider targeting interventions to people with specific psychosocial problems to boost clinical effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria related to psychosocial problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of inclusion criteria based on psychosocial problems was coded and found to moderate depression outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and report inclusion criteria related to psychosocial status; including participants with existing psychosocial problems can increase observed effects on depressive symptoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity and delivery (dose/adherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensity varied widely (one-day exercises to intensive therapy/coaching); adherence is often low in self-help interventions and affects effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report intensity/dose and adherence rates. Improve adherence via personalization, tailoring and interactive support; higher intensity/face-to-face interventions typically yield larger effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization/tailoring and interactive support
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalization, tailoring to individual needs and interactive support were recommended to improve adherence and effectiveness of (internet) self-help interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design self-help PPIs with personalization options and interactive/guided components to enhance adherence and outcome; report whether interventions were tailored or supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and adjustment for publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication bias was assessed (funnel plots, Orwin’s fail-safe N, Egger’s regression intercept) and corrected with Trim and Fill where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always assess publication bias using multiple methods (funnel plot asymmetry, fail-safe N, Egger's test) and, if indicated, adjust pooled estimates (e.g., Trim and Fill). Report adjusted effect sizes and imputed studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterogeneity assessment and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Heterogeneity was quantified (Q, I2, T2) and outliers were removed in sensitivity analyses to reduce heterogeneity and reassess effect sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Q, I2 and T2. Conduct sensitivity analyses (e.g., remove outliers) to evaluate robustness of pooled effects and report how heterogeneity influences interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect size and statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect sizes reported as Cohen's d with 95% CI, together with Z-values and p-values for overall effect tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report standardized effect sizes (Cohen’s d), 95% confidence intervals, Z and p-values for pooled and study-level effects. Include forest plots to visualize study estimates and weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analytic subgroup and moderator analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderator analyses examined self-selection, duration, type, recruitment, inclusion criteria, and quality rating to explain variability in effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify and report subgroup analyses and meta-regressions for plausible moderators. Test subgroup differences (Q-tests, slope/Z-statistics) and interpret cautiously when subgroup sizes are small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion criteria for meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict inclusion criteria were applied (e.g., excluded mindfulness/life-review therapies and school-based cluster randomized trials; excluded non peer-reviewed/grey literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and justify inclusion/exclusion criteria clearly. Be aware that excluding grey literature may increase risk of publication bias; consider trade-offs between strictness and comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and cultural generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Most studies were conducted in North America; the authors recommend replications in other countries/cultures because some positive psychology concepts may require adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report country/cultural context and consider cultural adaptation when implementing PPIs. Replicate studies across diverse settings before generalizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for clinical/public-health delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: For practice: deliver PPIs over longer periods (>=4 weeks, preferably >=8 weeks), on an individual basis for greater effectiveness; PPIs can be used in stepped care models and combined with other evidence-based approaches (mindfulness, ACT, behavioral activation, reminiscence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing PPIs in clinical or public-health contexts, prefer longer, individualized formats for clinical populations and consider self-help/internet formats for wide reach in stepped-care frameworks; monitor outcomes and escalate care if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for cost-effectiveness and broader impact evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors recommend cost-effectiveness studies to establish societal and public health impact and inform policy decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include economic evaluations and population impact modeling when possible to inform policy and resource allocation decisions about scaling PPIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for reporting trials (CONSORT adherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors recommend reporting randomized controlled trials according to the CONSORT statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to CONSORT guidelines (report randomization, allocation concealment, blinding where applicable, flow of participants, ITT analyses, etc.) to improve transparency and quality ratings.
